title: Multi-Partner Project: LoLiPoP-IoT - Design and Simulation of Energy-Efficient Devices for the Internet of Things
problem: IoT devices require extended battery life or energy autonomy; traditional approaches demand frequent battery replacement, creating maintenance burden and electronic waste.
motivation: Sustainable IoT demands reduced power consumption and energy harvesting integration; simulating solar cells and power circuits together is essential for design optimization.
method: Custom IoT localization tag design with integrated modeling of solar cells (from basic models to circuit integration) and electronics power consumption. Analyzes nRF52833 microcontroller and DW3110 ultra-wideband transceiver. Uses publicly available simulation tools. Optimizes power consumption with tradeoffs between photovoltaic panel area, lifespan, and localization latency.
key_novelty: Integrated simulation of solar harvesting and IoT electronics platform, demonstrating framework principles for modeling and optimizing energy-autonomous devices.
contributions: Solar panel area reduction for both 5-year lifespan and fully autonomous tags
Demonstration of firmware and hardware co-simulation using open tools
Optimization of power consumption with latency/panel-area tradeoffs
Practical framework for IoT energy-efficient design

metrics.other: reduced photovoltaic panel area for autonomous operation

limitations: Limited to specific nRF/DW3110 platform; generalization to other MCUs and transceivers not explored; field measurements absent.
primary_theme: energy-efficient IoT via solar harvesting simulation
